ideas.title: A whale swims through the ground (first look)
ideas.critique: The ground moves on its own as a travelling bulge that carries props and friends, and the island has never had that. The seesaw and the dunes already reshaped the terrain, though. If the riders only slide on a moving heightfield and the fluke is a canned pop-up, this reads as one more scripted island-wide event.

ideas.title: The pond's reflection goes on without us
ideas.critique: This is the shadow-quits gag again, with a reflection in place of the shadow, and that gag has already failed twice on film. The glass-clear dielectric pond is the only new thing in it, and a mirrored second set of bodies under the water is probably easier to fake than to read on screen.

ideas.title: The moon comes down to sleep on the beach
ideas.critique: A sky light falls onto the ground, rolls and lights the island from below, which is exactly the sun-ball recipe posted twice in a row. Swapping in the moon, night and leaves changes the props, not the idea.

ideas.title: Gravity holiday
ideas.critique: Gravity that points somewhere different for each creature, with walking upside down around a trunk, is a real new way things move, and the player feeling it is the strongest part. It sits right after the island's own-gravity ring, and if the poses snap or slide on the trunks it will look like broken physics, not a holiday.

ideas.title: The tide goes out a whole kilometre
ideas.critique: Moving the sea level to reveal or drown ground is the seesaw's payoff run backwards, and the sunken boat and stranded fish are generated props laid on a plain. The wet glossy floor and a wave the player can outrun are the only parts with something to play.

ideas.title: A friend turns to glass
ideas.critique: A clear refracting body with the island bent through it was the whole picture of the jelly-swallow film, and here it is a material swap on one creature. The focused caustic shadow and notes per tap are honest path tracer and sound work, but nothing happens in it beyond tapping.

ideas.title: Popcorn meadow
ideas.critique: A field that throws whoever stands on it, with puffs as physics particles and a dare-to-stand-still game, is something to play again and is unlike the recent films. It depends on the launches having weight and the puffs being a real particle system; a sprinkle of white blobs and a canned hop would sink it.

ideas.title: Lumi's dreams are visible
ideas.critique: Replaying the island inside a picture on the island is the TV's trick, now in a wobbly bubble over a sleeping Lumi. It does tie Lumi's real sleep to what it made, which is meaningful to the human, but as something to watch it is a small looping screen.

ideas.title: Crop letters for the human
ideas.critique: Friends lay out a word on the meadow to be read from above, which is the pebble-PIE recipe without the comic misreading that made that one land. Instanced tall grass that gets trampled is real rendering work, but the payoff is one still of text.

ideas.title: Everyone swaps voices
ideas.critique: Shuffling who says which lines is a table remap with a scripted chase, and the joke is used up the first time you hear it. Like the passed-along word, it lives in subtitles rather than in anything that moves or looks new.
